STILLROOT'S SONG   |   GM DOSSIER

Stillroot's Song

A refuge. A missing name. A song nobody admits hearing.

GM ONLY | 4-6 characters | Level 10 | 4-6 hours | Psychological folk horror

The party reaches Stillroot Hollow, usually shortened to Stillroot, carrying the body of Uppa Kase, their verdan bard. They survived a spirit troll. They need shelter, recovery and a priest, not another adventure. The village offers all three with a smile.

Behind the smile: Babha Yagha's coven is cultivating a dreambound false hydra beneath the village. Its song suppresses recognition; the coven edits the explanations people invent. Five murdered witnesses left physical evidence of a resistance network. Granny Nella, the apple-pie seller, is this edition's fixed dream-spy and the coven's local instrument. She is not the innocent Mrs. Halden.

Open these during play

You need... Open...

Your original monster numbers, not a rewrite @UUID[Compendium.stillroots-song-journals.gm-journals.JournalEntry.61d5f0fb7403f229]{Coven source stat blocks}

Five facts to keep beside you

The hags are Babha, Mama and Gahgah Yagha. Gahgah has two heads. The characters remain level 10, not level 15. Their current allowance is one rare item, two uncommon items and two standard healing potions each. Players keep their real notes: it is their characters' perceptions, not the table's trust, that are under attack.

Minimum viable session

Run the arrival, two murder sites, Nella's reveal, the dream entrance, one group nightmare trial, and the organ encounter. Use the remaining locations as alternate clue routes rather than compulsory stops. Do not attempt every optional encounter in one evening.

STILLROOT'S SONG   |   GM DOSSIER

Pacing and escalation

Segment Four-hour run Six-hour run Finish when...
Welcome, consent, party memories 15 min 20 min Each PC has one bond with Uppa.
Arrival, priest and genuine shelter 25 min 35 min The party has a reason to care and a secure base.
Investigation 50 min 85 min They identify an outside influence, a local agent and an underground focus.
Nella's betrayal and lucid crossing 20 min 30 min They choose how to enter the dream.
Dream dungeon 40 min 65 min They understand how the organ's stops work.
Finale 65 min 85 min The core is broken, or the party consciously retreats/bargains.
Dawn and debrief 25 min 40 min Consequences and each PC's closing moment are resolved.

These are table-time budgets, not required fictional travel times. A rest or resurrection ritual can be narrated in minutes of play. Include a comfort break by borrowing from investigation time; do not remove the ending.

Tension ladder

Comfort: a hot meal, dry cloth, practical kindness. Contradiction: two cups for a person living alone. Proof: a dated order signed by someone nobody knows. Threat: a reflection anticipates a gesture. Choice: save a witness or pursue a lead, with another route to either result. Agency: their tested countermeasure works. Confrontation: the monster can be faced because they learned its rules.

Use one conspicuous wrong detail per scene. In Form A, people are still people. If everything is visibly monstrous from the first minute, there is no normality to lose.

Pressure clock: the evening choir

Start at 0 of 6 after the party's first safe rest. Advance after a substantial excursion, a noisy confrontation, or a deliberately risky delay; announce an in-world symptom first. Never advance for real-life discussion, accessibility needs or breaks.

Step Observable change
1 Villagers repeat the same four-note phrase.
2 Reflections lag; an unattended ledger is being collected by Nella.
3 A known NPC starts sleepwalking toward the crystal path. Interception remains possible.
4 The chapel ward trembles; the shared-dream invitation becomes visible.
5 The false village briefly overlays the square. The finale begins with one extra loose memory echo.
6 The village falls into ritual sleep. The route remains open, but evacuation needs the core broken.

The clock never automatically kills a PC or makes the adventure unwinnable. At four hours, skip an optional room rather than speeding up the clock to punish the party.

STILLROOT'S SONG   |   GM DOSSIER

Canon and consolidation

This edition consolidates the adventure's development drafts into one playable reference. The author's established details take precedence over later draft inventions. New connective material is labelled as an editorial bridge or proposed ruling where it changes a practical outcome.

Topic Working canon Retired or optional material
Title Stillroot's Song The Song Beneath the Silence remains the working-title subtitle in old handouts.
Settlement Stillroot Hollow / Stillroot No new species conversion is imposed on the named villagers.
Party Level 10; 4-6 players; about 4-6 hours A later draft's escalation to level 15+ is not adopted.
Equipment One rare, two uncommon, two standard healing potions per PC Earlier very-rare allowance is superseded.
Ability scores Roll, using the GM's announced method Earlier point buy/standard array is superseded. No roll method was supplied.
Opening foe Spirit troll, described in the chat as CR 11 Crimson Wyrm is discarded.
Fallen companion Uppa Kase, verdan bard He is not a newly invented secret party member.
Coven Babha: Malevolent Matriarch; Mama: Venomous Fang; Gahgah: Tenebrous Troll Nethra, Grimma, Seranae and the later substituted titles are not used.
Inn Humblenook Inn; Jeb as proprietor Black Oak / Stillroot Rest are alternate draft names. Marcy Dunn is an unused innkeeper alternative.
Priest Reverend Ervin Hoss Father Tobin / Brightwood are draft alternatives, not extra priests.
Dream Warden Jonas Verstand Eldrin Fallow is an unused alternate; Elysia remains the elven chronicler.
Local spy Granny Nella, fixed before play Do not retroactively turn the players' favourite innocent into the spy.
Inn murder Antler-mounted victim Room for One remains an optional nightmare, not a second compulsory inn corpse.

Deliberate practical bridges

The original hags and mounts are retained as source stat blocks, with inconsistencies itemised separately. The default level-10 finale attacks their dream apparatus and projected hydra, not all three true hags and their mounts together. This is an encounter adaptation, not a silent reduction of their statistics.

The opening describes Uppa as terribly wounded but with essential remains recoverable. A previous draft's total dismemberment conflicts with a normal Raise Dead solution; the @UUID[Compendium.stillroots-song-journals.gm-journals.JournalEntry.9848b98a77681d3a.JournalEntryPage.b4f049079525ebfb]{resurrection notes} explain both versions.

The first safe rest is real. The party's opening depletion is not an excuse to deny them every class feature for six hours. House-rule ambiguities and a missing potion-toxicity table are explicitly identified in @UUID[Compendium.stillroots-song-journals.gm-journals.JournalEntry.ba872b141c8533da]{Rules}, not presented as previously agreed details.

Optional material preserved

The war-camp rescue, Ardeep library, Elysia's poems, the Aegis of Elara, Hekate adaptation, skeleton dance, giant's jail and both riddles are included as detachable journals. The empty d100 tables were templates, not encounters, and have not been padded with invented canon. The isolated '65 days until Kamras' egg hatches' note is retained in @UUID[Compendium.stillroots-song-journals.gm-journals.JournalEntry.a45d4f574d4d78a0]{Development archive}, not made into this adventure's clock.

STILLROOT'S SONG   |   GM DOSSIER

Horror without breaking table trust

Agree the intensity of body horror, dismemberment, harm involving children, memory interference and loss of control before play. Offer a plain 'pause', 'veil' or 'rewind' signal; no explanation is required. Naya and the war-camp captives are not murder victims in this edition. The detailed corpses are adults.

Tell players: 'Your character may misremember events. You, the player, may keep all your notes and compare them freely. Important discoveries will not depend on pretending to forget information.'

Collect one cherished memory, a regret the player is comfortable exploring, and one bond with Uppa. These are fictional prompts, not requests for personal trauma. A player can choose generic fear imagery instead.

Presentation

Use readable lighting, quiet ambience and silence deliberately. Do not use sudden extreme volume, flashing lights or actual sleep deprivation. Keep the horror in description. Give players concrete opportunities to investigate, interrupt danger and protect one another.

Fail forward

Essential clues are found when players examine the relevant thing. Checks provide precision, speed or additional leverage. A failed check does not erase the only route onward. Every key conclusion has at least three supporting clues in @UUID[Compendium.stillroots-song-journals.gm-journals.JournalEntry.66d06aa48fc28d63.JournalEntryPage.70b524c8443bc0fc]{the evidence matrix}.

End-of-session debrief

Ask which moment worked, which moment should be veiled next time, and what each character carries away from Stillroot. An optional lingering hum is atmosphere, not proof their successful actions were meaningless.
